purpose: Oseltamivir is used to treat the flu (influenza) in people who have had symptoms for no more than 2 days. It can also be used to help prevent the flu if you have been exposed to someone who has it. It works best when started as early as possible after symptoms begin.
how_it_works: The flu virus spreads in your body by making copies of itself and jumping from cell to cell. Oseltamivir blocks a tool the virus uses called neuraminidase, which the virus needs to escape from your cells and infect new ones. By blocking this tool, the medicine helps slow the spread of the virus so your body can fight it off more easily.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are nausea and vomiting, which usually happen within the first couple of days of taking the medicine. Taking it with food can help reduce stomach upset. Some people may also experience headache or stomach pain.
warnings: In rare cases, especially in children and teenagers, oseltamivir has been linked to unusual behavior or confusion. If you or your child seems confused, acts strangely, or has hallucinations, contact a doctor right away. People with kidney problems may need a lower dose, so be sure to tell your doctor about any kidney issues before taking this medicine.
typical_dosing: For treating the flu in adults, the usual dose is 75 mg taken twice a day (morning and evening) for 5 days. For flu prevention, it is typically 75 mg once a day for at least 10 days. Children are dosed based on their weight, so the doctor or pharmacist will calculate the right amount for your child.
